{{Top}}
{{Image}}
[[File:MC80_Assault_Cruiser_2016_Spring_Tournament_Kit.png|thumb|right|250px|A Mon Calamari Star Cruiser engages an Imperial Star Destroyer]]
{{Quote|Were you on a star-cruiser or a...?|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Star Cruiser''' was a widely used designation for spaceships in general<ref name="IV-V">{{Film|IV}}, [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].</ref> as well as a term for a prominent [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] warship production line, a series of Old Republic warships, and a subclass of large [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruisers]].

==History==
The term was sometimes used to describe spacecraft in general, and in this context, it was sometimes written in lowercase as '''star cruiser'''.<ref name="Marvel">[[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'' (1977)]]</ref><ref name="comic strip">[[Star Wars (comic strip)|''Star Wars'' comic strip]]</ref> The term could also be used to specify a type of large battlecruiser,<ref name="SW:CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref><ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and was used as designation for a series of Republic hammer-headed warships during the [[Great Galactic War]]<ref name="TOR:SW">{{SWArchive|url=games/videgames/tor_smugglersvanguard/index.html|text=''The Old Republic: Smuggler's Vanguard''|int=The Old Republic: Smuggler's Vanguard}}</ref> and, later, to describe a series of large Mon Calamari [[Warship/Legends|warships]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="RASB">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

===Republic usage===
The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] evidently used the term to describe their hammer-headed warships, like the [[Thranta-class corvette|''Thranta''-class corvette]], that were active in the Great Galactic War. The smuggler [[Hylo Visz]] knew them by this term, as she compared the [[Defender-class light corvette/Legends|''Defender''-class prototype]] to the larger, similar-looking vessels.<ref name="TOR:SW" />

===Calamari usage===
The famous [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruisers]] were the main [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. A typical Star Cruiser of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] was around 1200 m,<ref name="TEGTW" /> such as the iconic [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 ''Liberty'' type Star Cruiser]],<ref name="RASB" /> but the term could also apply to the 500 m [[Kuari Princess/Legends|''Kuari Princess'']], and to larger Mon Cal ships, like the [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']].<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Lowercase term===
The lowercase term "star cruiser" was also applied to [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] warships, where it was used as an alternate designation for [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]].<ref name="SOTG07">[[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'', Saga Edition]]</ref> It was also used as a synonym for the standard [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] designation, which referred to all combat warships above approximately 400 m in length, as for example the [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruiser]].<ref name="TCSWE" /> Smaller warships, like the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]], were also called this at times.<ref name="SWGQ">{{GalaxiesAED}} {{C|Quest Journal description for space mission "Kessel System: Seek and Destroy the Imperial Corvette"}}</ref>

===Battlecruiser class===
Some ships named with the uppercase "Star Cruiser" were bigger than standard Star Destroyer designs, and were large enough to be thought of as [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]]. They were an Imperial warship class separate from both Star Destroyers and Star Dreadnoughts,<ref name="ITW:OT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' refers to Rebel personnel using the term Star Cruiser for an Imperial warship type in-between Star Destroyers and Star Dreadnoughts in size and power.</ref><ref name="SBP1">In [[Starship Battles (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Starship Battles Preview 1'']], the Super Star Destroyer term itself is described as a colloquial outgrowth from the word Star Destroyer, which described the large dagger-shaped warships used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The same article states that Super Star Destroyer was a term applied to several different dagger-shaped [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] warship classes, making no mention of any Rebel ships being called this.</ref> considered by some to be a subtype of the battlecruiser class used in the [[Anaxes War College System/Legends|Anaxes War College System]]. Among many naval historians, any official inclusion of this subtype into their ship classification-system was debated and contested. A typical example of this Star Cruiser design was the [[Allegiance-class battlecruiser|''Allegiance''-class battlecruiser]], a 2200 m long model of Super Star Destroyer that was utilized by the Galactic Empire.<ref name="TEGTW" /> Likewise, the [[Secutor-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Secutor''-class Star Destroyer's]] length would technically have placed it under the Star Cruiser classification, but its comparative lack of armament, as well as its carrier-like role, qualified it as a Star Destroyer.

==Behind the scenes==
The term "star cruiser" first appeared in dialogue in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], written as "star-cruiser" and "starcruiser" in various versions of the script. Early [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] material such as [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel's ''Star Wars'' comics]] uses the term quite loosely, including for the ''Executor''. In the script for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes back'']], the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] is called a "Star Cruiser," with the words capitalized. Since [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], however, the term has been most widely used to describe [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruisers]].

In his endnotes for ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', Jason Fry mentioned that he had planned to give an explanation for [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] asking if [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] were on a Star Cruiser, but it was cut before the book was released. In addition, due to input from a [[TheForce.net]] test reader known only as Tzizvvt78, Fry placed the Star Cruiser line at the smaller end of the overall battlecruiser ship class. Fry liked the idea because it accounted for the continuity for Star Cruisers without sacrificing the [[West End Games]] cruiser ship classifications incorporated into the Anaxes War College System.<ref name="JFT">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24881617404/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-11|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 11}}</ref>
